name: Selective Context
executive_summary: Removes low self-information tokens from context to reduce length while preserving semantic content. Uses the LLM itself to score token importance and filters out redundant information.
description: Selective Context compresses prompts by computing the self-information (surprisal) of each token given its context. Tokens with low self-information (highly predictable, redundant) are candidates for removal. The algorithm iteratively removes the lowest-information tokens until a target compression ratio is reached. Unlike random truncation, this preserves the most semantically important content.
when_to_use: Long contexts that exceed model limits or increase cost.
When you need semantic-aware compression rather than random truncation.
RAG systems where retrieved documents are verbose.
when_not_to_use: When every token is potentially important (e.g., legal contracts).
When the model used for scoring differs from the generation model (distribution mismatch).
known_pitfalls: May remove implicitly important context that the scorer undervalues.
Compression ratio must be tuned per task.

primary_source.title: Compressing Context to Enhance Inference Efficiency of Large Language Models
